comments.author: somat
comments.why: Shows how Doble solved steam car startup in 1925
comments.text: Here is how they solved it in 1925. I feel with our many modern advancements we could do much better. [VIDEO] That said, as neat as steam cars are, there is a reason internal combustion engines won. Probably because they are smaller, lighter and most importantly cheaper.

comments.author: somat
comments.why: Doble as high point of steam car technology
comments.text: The stanly was a much earlier tech, perhaps the best car of it's generation. But compare that to the doble, perhaps the high point of steam car technology before that personal motive power route was abandoned. [VIDEO] Now admittedly the doble was a high end luxury item, But you can see how it could be possible to have a every mans steam car.

comments.author: dalke
comments.why: Mentions a handbook that came with a 1925 steam car
comments.text: 1930s isn't exactly ancient history. By 1930, for example, we had commercial aviation, a long-distance phone network, and experimental television stations. Of course we also had vacuum cleaners, steam engines, automobiles, combines, and all sorts of other things that needed manuals. At [VIDEO] you can hear mention of the manual that came with a 1925 steam car. ("In the handbook it says 'Things for your man to do every day.'") To be concrete, here's a copy of the instruction manual for a 51-P Crosley radio receiver from 1924: [LINK] . A "Manual of wireless telegraphy (radio) for the use of naval electricians" from 1915: [LINK] . And "A practical guide for the use of the Edison phonograph" from 1892: [LINK]
